nodes.label: F1 TV token is per browser tab
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.norm_label: f1 tv token is per browser tab
nodes.rationale: The token lives in sessionStorage, so the bookmarklet connects only the tab it was clicked in.

nodes.label: Bookmarklet reads login-session cookie
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.rationale: Connect F1 TV the MultiViewer way: bookmarklet reads the login-session cookie on formula1.com and returns to the app hash. No server-side password or token storage, per the user's request.

nodes.label: Reading F1 cookie from app page ruled out
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.norm_label: reading f1 cookie from app page ruled out
nodes.rationale: Cross-site cookie read is impossible without an extension; MultiViewer is Electron and reads it from its own BrowserWindow.

nodes.label: OAuth redirect back to app ruled out
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.norm_label: oauth redirect back to app ruled out
nodes.rationale: The account site's PingOne client only redirects to formula1.com, so an OAuth code cannot come back to localhost.

nodes.label: Live feed shares one token across pollers
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.norm_label: live feed shares one token across pollers
nodes.rationale: One shared live feed connection uses the last poller's token in memory, drops it when expired, and remembers a rejected token so pollers do not resend it every 5 s.

nodes.label: Full catalogue sweep gets IP blocked by F1 TV
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.norm_label: full catalogue sweep gets ip blocked by f1 tv
nodes.rationale: Hundreds of catalogue searches in minutes got every request 403'd by F1 TV and 429'd by Jolpica; probe a handful of races, not every race 1981-2026.

nodes.label: INTERNATIONAL feed sent with null channelId
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.norm_label: international feed sent with null channelid
nodes.rationale: CONTENT/PLAY with channelId answers 403 (1025 no data) on 2018-2024 races, while null plays the same international feed; null is safe on 2025/2026 too.

nodes.label: Shared glass surface recipe
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.rationale: One glass recipe (--glass, --glass-strong, --glass-blur, --hairline, --edge, --shadow) applied by a single selector list; new glass surfaces are added to that list, not restyled.

nodes.label: HUD and F1 TV viewer stay dark
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.norm_label: hud and f1 tv viewer stay dark
nodes.rationale: light-dark() resolves at the element using the token, so var(--glass) inside the dark-scheme 3D stage stays dark in light mode.

nodes.label: Page colours as light-dark() tokens on root
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.norm_label: page colours as light-dark() tokens on root
nodes.rationale: One token block defines every colour once with light-dark(); scheme chosen by color-scheme alone, giving auto/light/dark for free. Duplicated light overrides meant two places to sync per token. light-dark needs Chrome 123 / Safari 17.5 / Firefox 120.

nodes.label: 4K request retries in HD on refusal
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.norm_label: 4k request retries in hd on refusal
nodes.rationale: Pre-2025 videos refuse the x-f1-override-video-stream header (1033/1009 no 4K rights); play(uhd=True) retries without it. Error middle number is F1 TV's event id, last code gives cause.

nodes.label: Archive F1 TV videos play as HLS
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.norm_label: archive f1 tv videos play as hls
nodes.rationale: CONTENT/PLAY for archive content returns streamType HLS (H.264, 1080p max, 2010 race 576p25), so the 4K override header is ignored and the frontend must handle the t.hls path.

nodes.label: Hidden desktop pane throttles timers and rAF
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.norm_label: hidden desktop pane throttles timers and raf
nodes.rationale: When the user hides the pane, visibilityState becomes hidden: timers throttle to 1 s and rAF stops, so gap measurements are meaningless unless visibilityState is checked.

nodes.label: Reload pane after editing modules
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.rationale: A dynamic import() in the console returns the page's already-loaded old module, so location.reload() after edits.

nodes.label: Side from next-corner curvature ruled out
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.norm_label: side from next-corner curvature ruled out
nodes.rationale: Side from the inside of the next corner flips mid-pass on slow closing speeds, putting the passer across the other car (Abu Dhabi 2021).

nodes.label: Passer from current lap speed ruled out
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.norm_label: passer from current lap speed ruled out
nodes.rationale: Passer from len/lap time flips when one car crosses its lap boundary, again stacking two cars on one spot near the finish.

nodes.label: Pass side fixed per car pair
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.norm_label: pass side fixed per car pair
nodes.rationale: Side is a hash of the pair's ids so it never flips mid-pass; the passer is the car with higher steady median lap pace, so the faster car moves aside about 3.2 m.

nodes.label: Push-apart pass for lane chains
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.rationale: Without a final push-apart pass, chains (A passes B while B passes C) put two cars on the same side, as seen with bottas and leclerc on lap 1.

nodes.label: GPU ImageBitmap invalid after worker terminates
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.norm_label: gpu imagebitmap invalid after worker terminates
nodes.rationale: transferToImageBitmap from a GPU OffscreenCanvas in a worker is invalid after terminate (black ground, invalid mailbox GL warnings); satellite uses a CPU 2d canvas with willReadFrequently.

nodes.label: In-code timers instead of PerformanceObserver
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.rationale: performance.now() probes and a setInterval gap detector measured main-thread cost; PerformanceObserver longtask returned nothing in the desktop browser pane. Race switch dropped from 1.3-1.9 s blocked to 0.1-0.2 s.

nodes.label: Header Live button shows only while live
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.norm_label: header live button shows only while live
nodes.rationale: Its between-sessions Latest session label opened the race the default page already shows, so the button appears only during a live session.

nodes.label: Reserve drivers keep initials
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.rationale: FP1-only reserve drivers have no Wikipedia url in Jolpica, and guessing the article from the name could show the wrong person, so they keep initials.

nodes.label: Intro waits for showRace promise
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.rationale: startIntro waits for showRace (A.shown); starting earlier let showRace's late Press play hint land over the playing replay.

nodes.label: Stream rows load eagerly, three at a time
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.norm_label: stream rows load eagerly, three at a time
nodes.rationale: IntersectionObserver never fires while the browser is not painting (hidden preview pane), so rows sat on skeletons; every row is loaded three at a time instead.

nodes.label: Wikipedia portraits use pilicense any
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.rationale: Default free-images-only pageimages left out about half the 1950s grid, including champion Mike Hawthorn; pilicense any restores them.

nodes.label: Driver career positions from per-season standings
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.norm_label: driver career positions from per-season standings
nodes.rationale: Jolpica answers 400 without season_year on driverstandings, so career championship positions are built from each season's driverstandings table; results endpoint works without a season. Cold career (23 seasons) takes about 10 s, then cached.

nodes.label: Hidden pane freezes intro fade-in and camera
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.norm_label: hidden pane freezes intro fade-in and camera
nodes.rationale: In the hidden preview pane rAF barely runs, so the intro card stays at opacity 0 and the chase camera stays at overview; verify in a visible browser before calling it broken.

nodes.label: First-visit intro seeks to lap 1 start
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.norm_label: first-visit intro seeks to lap 1 start
nodes.rationale: A GPS replay starts about 90 s before lights out, so t=0 shows cars on the grid; intro starts at lap 1 start minus 6 s. Lap-timing replays have no laps feed and start at 0.

nodes.label: Writing JS via Python heredoc breaks escapes
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.norm_label: writing js via python heredoc breaks escapes
nodes.rationale: An escaped single quote inside a Python string does not come out as an escaped quote in JS; use double quotes in the JS instead.

nodes.label: Syntax-check frontend modules as ES modules
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.norm_label: syntax-check frontend modules as es modules
nodes.rationale: node --check passed a file the browser rejected; src/static has no package.json so Node treats files as CommonJS. Use node --input-type=module --check on stdin.

nodes.label: Formula 1 named only for facts
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.rationale: Formula 1 appears only where it states a fact, such as the footer's not-associated disclaimer and race data, keeping F1 out of the name and logo.

nodes.label: Lights Out trademark not yet checked
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.norm_label: lights out trademark not yet checked
nodes.rationale: Not checked whether Lights Out is already a trademark or domain for a similar product; check before going public.

nodes.label: App named Lights Out
nodes.author: ADITYA
nodes.rationale: The user chose Lights Out over F1 Data Browser because F1 is Formula 1's trademark; the name ties to the first-visit intro that opens at lights out. Slipstream, Parc Ferme and Box Box were rejected.

nodes.label: Vanilla JS ES-module frontend
nodes.rationale: Served as plain ES modules under /static with no build step.

nodes.label: Jolpica disk cache (SETTLED)
nodes.rationale: Jolpica allows about 500 requests per hour, so past seasons and settled races go through a disk cache.

nodes.label: Usage counts endpoint (/api/count)
nodes.rationale: Only per-day totals are kept: no id, cookie, IP or URL, and nothing is sent under Do Not Track or GPC.

nodes.label: server warm_up background thread
nodes.rationale: Fetches what the default page needs on parallel threads and builds the last 3 races' GPS replays at start-up so first play does not wait.

nodes.label: Replay control bar menus
nodes.rationale: The replay bar had 18 controls; menus cut it to 6 in replay and 4 in Simulate.

nodes.label: Season GPS warm-up and lap-timing fallback
nodes.norm_label: season gps warm-up and lap-timing fallback
nodes.rationale: An uncached GPS replay took up to a minute; the lap-timing replay now plays meanwhile and hands over to GPS mid-race.

nodes.label: Phone tab bar edge fade
nodes.rationale: At 375 px only three of seven tabs showed with no hint of more; a scroll-driven fade signals them.

nodes.label: Replay kind tags in race picker
nodes.norm_label: replay kind tags in race picker
nodes.rationale: Pre-1996 races used to fail only after pressing play, so each race is tagged with what play gives.

nodes.label: Return-visit notice and next-session countdown
nodes.rationale: Returning visitors had no reason to come back; a notice for an unseen race and a countdown give one.

nodes.label: Seven-tab reorganization
nodes.rationale: Strategy lab and the 3D replay are the features only this app has, so they lead the tabs; qualifying became a toggle in Results.

nodes.label: Usage events and /api/counts
nodes.rationale: Nothing was measured; first-party event counts give a view of the changes with no third party involved.

nodes.label: UX audit: first visit and conversion
nodes.norm_label: ux audit: first visit and conversion

nodes.label: Realistic kerb placement (apex inside, exit outside)
nodes.norm_label: realistic kerb placement (apex inside, exit outside)

nodes.label: Existing PBR render pipeline (HDRI, CSM, MSAA, bloom)
nodes.norm_label: existing pbr render pipeline (hdri, csm, msaa, bloom)

nodes.label: livef1 dead ends
nodes.rationale: Old F1 livetiming endpoints return 401 and the f1.com results scrape 404s, so the newer /signalrcore feed is used instead.

nodes.label: OpenF1 free-tier rate limit
nodes.rationale: OpenF1 free tier is about 30 requests a minute, so one GPS replay (about 30 requests) is expensive and is built one at a time.

nodes.label: Lap-timing replay (1996 onwards)
nodes.rationale: Pre-2023 races have no GPS, so cars are placed by average lap pace and are exact only at the start/finish line.

nodes.label: OpenF1 locked during live sessions
nodes.rationale: OpenF1 refuses free requests for every session while any session is live, so cached replays are the only fallback.

nodes.label: First-visit intro card
nodes.rationale: A first-time visitor should watch a race replay and come back, so the intro shows the product before the chrome.

nodes.label: Three-way view switch
nodes.rationale: Two side-by-side segmented controls read as one confusing control, so they were merged into one three-way switch.

nodes.label: Race views (calendar, results, qualifying, lap chart, standings)
nodes.norm_label: race views (calendar, results, qualifying, lap chart, standings)

nodes.label: F1 TV connect bar on Stream
nodes.norm_label: f1 tv connect bar on stream
nodes.rationale: Playback needs the viewer's F1 TV account, so the failure moved from the player to a connect bar up front.

nodes.label: Rename to Lights Out
nodes.rationale: The old name sounded like a developer tool and led with Formula 1's trademark; a trademark check is still pending.

nodes.label: CC BY 4.0 licence
nodes.rationale: Project code licence does not cover model files; each keeps its own licence

nodes.label: Load-time livery repaint (team colour, nose number, rain light)
nodes.norm_label: load-time livery repaint (team colour, nose number, rain light)
nodes.rationale: Replaces the Red Bull livery so one model serves every team; also splits per-corner wheels, steering wheel, sprung body and reflective mirror glass

nodes.label: Live GPS needs F1 TV
nodes.rationale: F1 withholds live car positions and telemetry unless a subscription token is supplied.

nodes.label: Learnings directory
nodes.rationale: Learnings are short summaries, never transcripts, so the committed folder stays small and readable.

nodes.label: Replay cache in .cache/replay
nodes.rationale: Finished GPS replays are cached on disk; delete them after changing the payload format; saves are atomic and concurrent requests wait on a lock.
